sedí: seer — he was (staying), was (imperfect 3rd sg. in -í, beside sedié; Pidal's se[d]í, the d restored; seer 'to sit', here simply 'to be, abide'; = estaba)
yazies: yazer + se — he was lying (down) (yazie, imperfect 3rd sg., + enclitic se; Pidal 'estábase echado'; = yacía, estaba echado)
durmie: dormir — he was sleeping (imperfect 3rd sg., -ie ending; = dormía)
sobrevienta: sobrevienta — sudden mishap, unlooked-for event (noun, from sobrevenir 'to befall'; mala sobrevienta, Pidal 'mala sorpresa'; closest imprevisto, percance)
cuntió: cuntir — it happened, befell (preterite 3rd sg.; que les cuntió 'that befell them', Pidal 'les aconteció'; = aconteció)
saliós: salir + se — it got out, broke out (salió, preterite 3rd sg., + enclitic reflexive se, its -e dropped; of the lion; = se salió)
red: red — grating, cage (fem. noun; Pidal 'reja, jaula'; here the lion's cage; modern red 'net')
desatós: desatar + se — it got loose, broke free (desató, preterite 3rd sg., + enclitic reflexive se; of the lion; = se desató)
çercan: çercar — they surround, encircle (present 3rd pl.; = cercan; ç sounded ts)
ferrant: Ferrant — Fernando (personal name; Pidal's Ferran[t]; Ferrant Gonçalvez, one of the two Infantes of Carrión; = Fernando)
gonçalvez: Gonçalvez — González, 'son of Gonçalvo' (patronymic; Ferrant Gonçalvez, Diag Gonçalvez; = González)
ifant: ifant — infante, young nobleman, son of a noble house (sg., ifante with its final -e dropped; ifant de Carrión, restored by Pidal; = infante)
alçasse: alçar(se) — (where) he might hide, take cover (imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg.; dos alçasse = do 'where' + se + alçasse, Pidal 'donde se escondiese'; modern alzar 'to lift')
abierta: abrir — open (past part. fem. sg., agreeing with cámara; = abierta)
metiós: meter + se — he put himself, got himself in(to), hid (metió, preterite 3rd sg., + enclitic reflexive se; = se metió)
esçaño: escaño — bench, long seat with a back (variant spelling with ç of escaño; masc. sg.; = escaño)
diag: Diag — Diego (personal name, Diago with its final -o dropped; Pidal's Di[a]g; Diag Gonçalvez, one of the two Infantes of Carrión; = Diego)
viga: viga — beam, timber (fem. noun; viga lagar 'the beam of a press', the two nouns in apposition; = viga)
lagar: lagar — wine or oil press, press-house (masc. noun; = lagar); in viga lagar the pair is read as 'press-beam', reading from context
brial: brial — tunic, long silk garment worn by nobles (masc. noun; no modern word in use, closest túnica)
çercado: çercar — surrounded (past part. masc. sg., agreeing with escaño; = cercado)
qués: qué + es — what is (interrogative qué + es, 'is', run together; qués esto 'what is this'; = qué es)
levantó: levantar — he raised, got up (preterite 3rd sg.; with reflexive se, se levantó 'he stood up'; = levantó)
cuello: cuello — neck (= cuello; al cuello 'about his neck' of a mantle worn, and 'by the neck', al cuello lo tomó, Pidal 'lo cogió por el cuello')
envergonçó: envergonçar — he was abashed, cowed (preterite 3rd sg., read here as intransitive/reflexive without se; closest se avergonzó; sense taken from context)
premió: premer — it pressed down, lowered (preterite 3rd sg.; la cabeça premió, Pidal 'bajó la cabeza'; Latin premere; closest apretar, bajar; not modern premiar 'to reward')
liévalo: levar + lo — he leads it, takes it along (lieva, present 3rd sg. of levar, + object lo, the accent marking the stress; = lo lleva)
adestrando: adestrar — leading (as a horse is led) by the halter (gerund; from diestro 'right hand'; Pidal 'lo lleva como de diestro'; closest llevar del diestro)
llamando: llamar — calling (gerund; están llamando 'they are calling'; = llamando)
color: color — colour; sin color 'colourless, pale' (= color)
juego: juego — game, sport; here jesting, mockery at the Infantes' expense (masc. noun; tal juego commo iva por la cort 'such sport as went round the court', which the Cid forbids; = juego, burla)
enbaídos: enbaído — shamed, put out of countenance (past part. masc. pl. of enbaír; Pidal 'avergonzados, corridos')
búcar: Búcar — Búcar, the Moorish king who comes against Valencia (personal name, Arabic; no modern Spanish form beyond Búcar)
oviestes: aver — you had (strong preterite 2nd pl.; = hubisteis); sil oviestes contar 'if you have heard tell of him', Pidal 'si oísteis de él' (sil = si + le)
catamos: catar — we looked at, considered (preterite 1st pl., the same form as the present; Pidal 'miramos', of the time of the marriage; = miramos, consideramos)
bibdas: bibda — widows (fem. pl., with b for v; = viudas)
remandrán: remaner — they will remain, be left (future 3rd pl., syncopated remanrán with a d grown between n and r; = quedarán)
desean: desear — they long for, desire (present 3rd pl.; = desean)
idlos: ir + los — go (id, imperative 2nd pl. of ir; = id) + los, object of the next verb conortar; idlos conortar 'go and comfort them' (= id a consolarlos)
conortar: conortar — to comfort, encourage, cheer (infinitive; = confortar, consolar)
ayan: aver — (that) they have (present subjunctive 3rd pl.; = hayan); non ayan i raçión 'let them have no share in it'
raçión: raçión — share, portion (fem. noun; non ayan i raçión, Pidal 'no tomen parte en la batalla'; closest parte; not the modern 'ration')
vençremos: vençer — we shall defeat, overcome (future 1st pl., syncopated from vençer + emos; = venceremos)
tenedes: tener — you hold, have (present 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = tenéis)
blancas: blanco — white (fem. pl., agreeing with fijas; = blancas)
desseo: dessear — I desire, long for (present 1st sg.; = deseo)
folgad: folgar — rest, take your ease, enjoy yourselves (imperative 2nd pl.; = holgad, from holgar)
trevo: trever(se) — I dare (present 1st sg.; = me atrevo; arrancar me los trevo 'I dare to rout them', Pidal 'me atrevo a vencerlos': me is the reflexive of treverse, set before the infinitive)

__broaden__.valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia) · also Valençia — the city itself, held by the Cid (en Valençia sedí mio Çid 'in Valencia was my Cid'; Valençia vienen çercar 'they come to besiege Valencia')
__broaden__.de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment') · also de — 'with, from' of the means or source (diziendo de la boca 'saying with his mouth'; de cuer les pesa 'it grieves them from the heart') · also de que 'of whom, of which' (relative after a noun; de moros de que non avien sabor 'of Moors they had no taste for')
__broaden__.león: León — León, the kingdom and city (Alfons el de León 'Alfonso of León'; = León) · also león — lion, the animal (masc.; saliós … el león 'the lion broke loose', adeliñó para' león 'he made straight for the lion'; = león), not the kingdom
__broaden__.enbraçan: enbraçar — to take (the shield) on the arm by its straps (present 3rd pl.; enbraçan los escudos 'they take their shields on their arms'; = embrazan) · also enbraçar — to wind (the mantle) round the arm as a shield (enbraçan los mantos 'they wrap their cloaks on their arms')
__broaden__.fincan: fincar — they stop, cease (present 3rd pl.; non fincan de andar 'they do not stop riding'; = quedan, closest cesan) · also fincar — they stay, take their stand (fincan sobre so señor 'they take their stand around their lord'; = se quedan, se plantan)
__broaden__.sobre: sobre — upon, over; here 'on the security of' (sobre aquellas arcas) · sobre Navas de Palos 'above, hard by Navas de Palos' (position along the route) · also 'before, against (a town to be besieged)' (sobre Alcoçer iva posar 'went to camp before Alcocer') · also sobre — 'besides, in addition to' (Sobre aquesto todo 'on top of all this') · also sobre — around (Pidal 'alrededor de', comp. v. 1053; fincan sobre so señor 'they stand around their lord')
__broaden__.dos: dos — two · also do + se, 'when/where … (they)' (Dos fallan con los moros 'when they come upon the Moors', Pidal 'cuando se encuentran'; = cuando se encuentran) · also do + se, 'where … (he might)' with a subjunctive (non vido … dos alçasse 'he saw nowhere he might hide', Pidal 'donde se escondiese')
__broaden__.sol: sol — sun · also 'even, so much as' (sol non 'not even'; sol non será penssado 'it will not even be thought of') · also sol — so + l, 'under the' (so 'under', Latin sub, + el before a vowel): del sol espada 'from under the sword' (the likeliest reading; the construction is uncertain) · also Sol — doña Sol, one of the Cid's two daughters (personal name) · also sol — so + el, 'under the' (metiós sol esçaño 'he got under the bench'; here the sense is clear)
__broaden__.ovo: aver — he had (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = hubo; here perfect auxiliary, ovo bastidos = 'he had furnished') · ovo de + inf., little more than a plain past (las manos se ovo de untar 'his hands were smeared'); dont a ojo los ovo 'as soon as he had them in sight' · also aver — he had, possessed, felt (plain verb of possession with a noun object; tanto ovo el pavor 'so great was the fear he had')
__broaden__.todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision') · also todo — adverbial 'wholly, all over' before an adjective (todo suzio 'all filthy')
__broaden__.assí: assí — thus, so (= así) · also assí — so greatly, so much (Pidal 'de tal modo, mucho'; assí envergonçó 'was so abashed')
__broaden__.maravilla: maravilla — wonder, marvel (noun; = maravilla) · also aver a maravilla — to marvel at, hold a wonder (a maravilla lo han 'they marvel at it')
__broaden__.tornáronse: tornar + se — they turned, set (to) (tornaron, preterite 3rd pl., + reflexive se; tornáronse a armar 'they set to arming themselves again'; = se volvieron) · also tornar + se — they went back, returned (tornáronse al palaçio 'they went back to the palace')
__broaden__.tal: tal — such; por tal 'for such a reason, for this purpose' (= tal) · also tal … commo — 'such … as' (tal juego commo iva por la cort 'such sport as went round the court')
__broaden__.tovieron: tener — they held, handled (strong preterite 3rd pl.; tovieron armas 'they played at arms' in the games, Pidal 'jugaron las armas'; cf. tenien armas; = tuvieron) · also tener por — to hold as, consider (tovieron por enbaídos 'they held (them) shamed')
__broaden__.fiera: fiero — fierce, rugged, wild (fem.; la sierra que fiera es 'the range, which is rugged'; = fiera, fem. of fiero) · also fiera cosa — adverbial, 'fiercely, greatly' (fiera cosa les pesa 'it weighs on them terribly'; Pidal 'fieramente, mucho')
__broaden__.cuer: cuer — heart (Latin cor; = corazón) · also de cuer — from the heart, deeply (de cuer les pesa 'it weighs on them deeply')
__broaden__.part: part — share, portion (noun; = parte) · also part — side (del otra part 'on the other side'; = parte) · also a part — aside, apart (a part salidos son 'they have gone aside')
__broaden__.sabidor: sabidor — one who knows, informed, in charge (= sabedor; vos seed sabidor 'you be the judge, the one who decides') · also sabidor de — acquainted with, familiar with (d' aquellos moros yo so sabidor 'I know those Moors well')
__broaden__.arrancar: arrancar — to drive off, rout (infinitive; a arrancar 'to be routed', passive-reflexive sense, cf. arrancada 'rout'; = ser derrotado, ahuyentado; modern arrancar 'to pull up, start') · also arrancar la lid — to win the battle, drive the foe from the field, active (yo la he de arrancar 'I must win it'; = ganar) · also arrancar + object — to rout, defeat (active; arrancar me los trevo 'I dare to rout them', Pidal 'me atrevo a vencerlos')
